segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For since the law has a shadow of the good things to come and not the form itself of the realities, it can never, by the same sacrifices that they offer perpetually year after year, make perfect those who draw near.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered, since the worshippers, cleansed once for all, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But in those sacrifices there is a reminder of sins year after year,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, when he comes into the world, he says:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Sacrifice and offering you did not want, but a body you prepared for me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In whole burnt offerings and sin offerings you took no pleasure.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then I said, ‘See, I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about me—to do your will, O God.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After saying above,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sin offerings you did not want, nor did you take pleasure in them,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: these being offered according to the law,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he then said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “See, I have come to do your will.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He does away with the first in order to establish the second.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: By that will we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And every priest stands day after day ministering and offering again and again the same sacrifices, which can never remove sins.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But this one, having offered a single sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: waiting from then on until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for by a single offering he has made perfect for all time those who are being made holy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws on their hearts, and I will write them on their minds,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he adds,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “and their sins and their lawless acts I will remember no more.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, brothers and sisters, since we have confidence for entry into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: an entry he inaugurated for us as a new and living way through the curtain, that is, his flesh,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for the one who promised is faithful.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And let us pay attention to one another, to stir up love and good works,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: not abandoning our own meeting together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if we go on sinning deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but a fearful expectation of judgment and the fury of a fire that is about to consume the adversaries.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Anyone who has set aside the law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: How much worse a punishment do you think someone will be judged to deserve who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, treated as profane the blood of the covenant by which he was made holy, and insulted the Spirit of grace?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For we know the one who said,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and again,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “The Lord will judge his people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But remember the earlier days, when, after you were enlightened, you endured a hard contest of sufferings,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: sometimes being made a public spectacle through insults and afflictions, and sometimes becoming partners of those who were treated that way.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For you sympathized with the prisoners and accepted the plundering of your possessions with joy, knowing that you yourselves have a better possession, one that lasts.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For you need endurance, so that after doing the will of God you may receive what was promised.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “yet a very little while, and the one who is coming will come and will not delay;

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: but my righteous one will live by faith, and if he shrinks back, my soul takes no pleasure in him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But we are not of those who shrink back to destruction, but of those who have faith to the preserving of the soul.

notes.note: The Greek word usually means 'image' or 'likeness', but here it is set against 'shadow' and denotes the real shape of the thing, not a copy of it. 'Image' would suggest to a modern reader a second kind of copy, which is the opposite of the point. Several recent translations likewise use 'true form'.

notes.phrase: a body you prepared for me
notes.note: The quotation is Psalm 40:6–8 in its Greek (Septuagint) form, which the author hears as words spoken by Christ on entering the world. The Hebrew text of the psalm reads 'ears you have dug for me' at this point; the author's argument in verse 10 depends on the Greek wording, 'a body'.

The verb means to set apart as belonging to God, and it is the verbal form of the ordinary word 'holy'. 'Sanctified' is accurate but hides that connection and has acquired a specialised sense of gradual moral improvement that is not the point here. Some modern translations also use 'made holy'.

The phrase can be attached either to what precedes ('offered a single sacrifice for sins for all time') or to what follows ('sat down for all time at the right hand of God'). The Greek word order allows both and interpreters are divided. The rendering here takes it with the sacrifice, matching verse 14; the seated posture, in contrast to the priests who 'stand' in verse 11, makes the point of finished work on either reading.

The Greek has no words corresponding to 'he adds'; the sentence that begins 'after saying' in verse 15 is never formally completed. Most interpreters and translations take verse 17 as the point where it resumes and supply a phrase like this, as some later manuscripts also do. A minority take 'says the Lord' in verse 16 as the resumption. The quotation is from Jeremiah 31:33–34.

The Greek plural was the normal way to address a mixed group of men and women as fellow members of a family or community. 'Brothers' alone now suggests to English readers that only men are addressed. Many recent translations make the same choice.

The Greek is a plural, 'the holy things' or 'holy places', used in Hebrews for the sanctuary, and here for its innermost room behind the curtain. Under the law only the high priest entered it, once a year on the Day of Atonement, carrying sacrificial blood. The author applies this to the heavenly presence of God, now open to all worshippers.

Grammatically 'his flesh' most naturally explains 'the curtain', so that Jesus' body, given in death, is what was passed through to open the way. Some interpreters instead attach it to 'way' (the new and living way consisting in his flesh), finding it awkward to compare his body to a barrier. The rendering leaves the phrase where the Greek has it; the first reading is the majority view.

The law distinguished unintentional sins, for which sacrifices were provided, from defiant, 'high-handed' sin, for which there was none (Numbers 15:22–31). The author draws on that distinction. The context (verse 29) shows that he has in view a knowing repudiation of Christ, not every conscious lapse.

Some manuscripts read 'my chains' in place of 'the prisoners', which is the reading behind the King James Version and was once used as evidence that Paul wrote the letter. The reading 'the prisoners' is judged original by nearly all modern editors.

notes.phrase: my righteous one will live by faith
notes.traditional: the just shall live by faith
notes.note: Verses 37–38 combine a phrase from Isaiah 26:20 with Habakkuk 2:3–4 in a Greek form, with the clauses reordered so that 'shrinks back' applies to the righteous person. The Greek word translated 'faith' also means 'faithfulness', and in this context of endurance under pressure both senses are in play; the Hebrew of Habakkuk reads 'by his faithfulness'. 'Righteous' and 'just' translate the same Greek word.

candidates.reason: A key term in Hebrews (and in John and Paul) where 'perfect', 'complete', and 'bring to its goal' are all defensible and readers will be misled if the English varies between chapters.
Translators split between 'sanctify', 'make holy', and 'consecrate', and the choice should match the register's handling of ἅγιος across the New Testament.
Recurs in John, Acts, Paul, Hebrews and 1 John with renderings varying among 'boldness', 'confidence', 'openness', and 'plainly'; the senses need to be fixed once.
The plural address occurs throughout the letters and Acts, and whether to render it inclusively needs a single policy.
Ranges over 'life', 'self', and 'soul' across the New Testament; 'soul' can mislead modern readers, and the choice between them should be made consistently.
